name: Giant Chocolate Chip Cookies
desc: Tessa Arias's quarter-pound cookies: cold butter, no chill, crisp edge and gooey middle.

source.title: Giant Chocolate Chip Cookies
source.evidence: Tessa Arias's recipe: same cold cubed butter, 380 g flour base, 150 g granulated and 250 g light brown sugar, chips plus reserved chunks, 113 g balls at 375°F; this version adds 16 g flour for Salt Lake altitude.

ingredients.raw: 3 cups plus 2 tbsp (396 g) all-purpose flour (380 g plus 16 g for altitude)
ingredients.note: 396 g; 380 g plus 16 g for altitude

ingredients.raw: 1 cup (2 sticks, 227 g) cold unsalted butter, cubed, straight from the fridge
1 1/4 cups (250 g) packed light brown sugar
1 cup (170 g) semisweet chocolate chunks, hand-chopped from a bar, divided

steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F. Line two large baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, whisk the flour, fine sea salt, baking powder and baking soda.

In a stand mixer, beat the cold butter, granulated sugar and brown sugar on low, increasing to medium-high, until well combined and fluffy, 3-4 minutes. Cold butter takes longer than soft; do not swap in softened butter, cold is what keeps these thick.
Add the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla, beating until combined.
On low speed, add the flour mixture gradually, mixing only until combined. Beat in the chocolate chips and half the chunks.

Weigh 113 g (4 oz) portions and roll into even balls; this dough runs closer to 1/2 cup per portion, so a scale beats a scoop. Place 6 per pan, spaced far apart, and press the remaining chunks into the tops.

Bake 15-20 minutes, until the edges are browned and the cookies are puffy. For crispy edges, check at 17 and pull around 18 to 19 when the edge ring is golden brown. Less time is gooier, more time crispier.
Sprinkle with flaky salt right out of the oven. The cookies deflate slightly as they cool; let them set on the pan before moving.
tips: The 2 tbsp (16 g) flour above Tessa's 380 g is an altitude adjustment for Salt Lake City; at sea level use 3 cups (380 g).
Handle the Heat's own range is 15 to 20 minutes. Best the day they are baked; they keep 2 days airtight.
